## Morning — Foundations and Benchmarking Practice

### Tobias Wiesenthal

**Title/session:** Opening and workshop framing

Tobias Wiesenthal is Head of Unit for Digital Health (JRC.F.7) at the European
Commission's Joint Research Centre. His public research profile links him to JRC
work in research policy, innovation and digital health-related publications.

Bio source: sourced from public internet information:
[EU Whoiswho](https://op.europa.eu/en/web/who-is-who/person/-/person/COM_000004CA7)
and [ResearchGate](https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Tobias-Wiesenthal).

### Marusca Gnecchi

**Title/session:** Opening and workshop framing

Marusca Gnecchi is Deputy Head of the Centre for Advanced Studies at the European
Commission's Joint Research Centre. Public JRC-related material describes the
Centre for Advanced Studies as an incubator for forward-looking,
trans-disciplinary research and strategic networks.

Bio source: sourced from public internet information:
[LinkedIn profile](https://it.linkedin.com/in/marusca-gnecchi-83727649) and a
[JRC-related LinkedIn post](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/jolita-butkevi%C4%8Dien%C4%97-444786156_airp-vacancies-all-activity-7467545669055213568-T8YT).

### Vedran Dunjko

**Title:** The Provable Frontier of Quantum Machine Learning

Vedran Dunjko is Professor of Quantum Computing at Leiden University's computer
science institute, the Leiden Institute of Advanced Computer Science, in close
collaboration with the Leiden Institute of Physics. He works on quantum
algorithms, quantum machine learning and AI for quantum computing, and co-founded
the Applied Quantum Algorithms Leiden initiative.

Bio source: sourced from public internet information:
[Leiden University](https://www.medewerkers.universiteitleiden.nl/nieuws/2023/11/nieuwe-professor-vedran-dunjko-zoekt-problemen-uit-de-echte-wereld-die-een-quantumcomputer-kan-oplossen)
and [LIACS](https://liacs.leidenuniv.nl/~dunjkov/).

### Miguel A. González Ballester

**Title:** Quantum computing for interpretable AI in healthcare

Miguel A. González Ballester is an ICREA Research Professor at Universitat Pompeu
Fabra, founder of BCN Medtech, and a specialist in medical image analysis,
surgical technologies and quantum machine learning for healthcare. His career
includes senior research and leadership roles at Toshiba Medical Systems, INRIA,
the University of Bern and Alma IT Systems, with extensive publications,
supervision and international conference leadership.

Bio source: extracted from information sent by the speaker.

### Federico Ricci-Tersenghi

**Title:** Spin glass models are good benchmarks for discrete combinatorial optimization

Federico Ricci-Tersenghi is Professor of Theoretical Physics at Sapienza
University of Rome, working on the statistical physics of strongly disordered
systems, including spin glasses, structural glasses, constraint satisfaction,
optimization and inference problems. He completed his PhD at Sapienza under
Giorgio Parisi and has held visiting positions at several major international
institutes.

Bio source: sourced from public internet information:
[Sapienza PhD programme profile](https://phd.uniroma1.it/web/FEDERICO-RICCI-TERSENGHI_nC148_IT.aspx)
and [Ricerc@Sapienza](https://research.uniroma1.it/researcher/2e2e000e112e921bceee41635ebe0b533384d73ac5d71d45b716df80).

### Daniel J. Egger

**Title:** The Quantum Optimization Benchmarking Library

Daniel J. Egger is a Senior Research Scientist in the Quantum Applications
Research & Software group at IBM Research Europe - Zurich. His research focuses on
quantum information processing with superconducting circuits, pulse-level control
of quantum systems and quantum algorithms, including quantum optimization.

Bio source: sourced from public internet information:
[IBM Research](https://research.ibm.com/people/daniel-egger) and
[IBM Quantum](https://www.ibm.com/quantum/blog/quantum-optimization-benchmarking).

## Afternoon — Use Cases, First Session

### Zev Kronenberg

**Title:** Developing a genomic standard using the Platinum Pedigree

Zev Kronenberg is Associate Director of Computational Biology at PacBio, where he
works on genomic benchmarking and variant analysis using highly accurate long-read
DNA sequencing. He trained as a postdoctoral researcher with Evan Eichler at the
University of Washington after completing his PhD at the University of Utah.

Bio source: extracted from information sent by the speaker.

### Aurora Maurizio

**Title:** Where genomics resists quantum speedup: a biologist's POV

Aurora Maurizio is a computational biologist and bioinformatician at the Center
for Omics Sciences / Center for Translational Genomics and Bioinformatics at IRCCS
Ospedale San Raffaele in Milan. Her background includes functional and structural
genomics, transposable-element-mediated structural variants, and high-performance
computing for biological data.

Bio source: sourced from public internet information:
[San Raffaele](https://research.hsr.it/en/centers/omics-sciences/aurora-maurizio.html)
and [Frontiers Loop](https://loop.frontiersin.org/people/2188359/bio).

### Miguel Ponce de Leon

**Title:** Hard Optimization Problems in Mechanistic Biology

Miguel Ponce de Leon is a researcher in the Life Sciences Department at the
Barcelona Supercomputing Center, working at the intersection of computational
systems biology, complex systems, epidemiology, data science and AI. His work
includes multiscale models of cancer and cellular signalling, large-scale
simulations and HPC-based model exploration workflows.

Bio source: sourced from public internet information:
[personal website](https://miguel-pdl.com/) and
[EMBL-EBI training material](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/training/materials/permedcoe-summer-school/trainer-biographies/).

### Carlo Mancini Terracciano

**Title:** From Neural Network Dose Estimation to Clinically Constrained Plans: Radiotherapy Treatment Planning as a Benchmark for Hybrid Optimization

Carlo Mancini Terracciano is a researcher in Sapienza University's Applied
Radiation Physics Group, with a background in particle physics and a PhD from Roma
Tre. His work includes hadrontherapy-related modelling and benchmarking, including
carbon-ion breakup models and instrumentation for tumour resection using beta-minus
radio tracers.

Bio source: sourced from public internet information:
[Sapienza Applied Radiation Physics Group](https://arpg.sbai.uniroma1.it/index.php/research-group/permanentstaff).

### Gabriele Spada

**Title:** Quantum Molecular Docking with Neutral Atoms at CINECA

Gabriele Spada is a Quantum Computing Specialist at CINECA in Bologna, working on
quantum-classical integration and hybrid quantum applications in national and
European projects. His background is in theoretical particle physics and
computational quantum physics, including quantum Monte Carlo simulations and
ultracold atom systems.

Bio source: extracted from information sent by the speaker.

## Afternoon — Use Cases, Second Session

### Hao Wang

**Title:** What Are We Really Benchmarking? Toward Credible Evaluation of Quantum Optimization

Hao Wang is an assistant professor at the Leiden Institute of Advanced Computer
Science, Leiden University, working on optimization, benchmarking and performance
analysis of stochastic optimization algorithms. He is co-editor-in-chief of the
Evolutionary Computation Journal and has received major recognition including the
PPSN 2016 best paper award and the NeurIPS 2020 black-box optimization
competition prize.

Bio source: extracted from information sent by the speaker.

### Guglielmo Mazzola

**Title:** From Asymptotic Speedups to Practical Quantum Advantage

Guglielmo Mazzola is Associate Professor at SISSA and a computational
condensed-matter physicist developing Monte Carlo and quantum Monte Carlo
algorithms for classical and quantum computers. His research covers practical
quantum advantage, quantum algorithms for sampling, optimization, chemistry,
genomics and finance, and the limitations of textbook speedups under realistic
constraints.

Bio source: sourced from public internet information:
[SISSA profile](https://cm.sissa.it/people/guglielmo-mazzola) and
[SISSA course page](https://cm.sissa.it/node/387).

### Francesco Zamponi

**Title:** Machine-Learning-Enhanced Monte Carlo for Combinatorial Optimization and Sampling

Francesco Zamponi is a theoretical physicist at the Department of Physics of
Sapienza University of Rome, working on the statistical mechanics of disordered
and complex systems, including glasses, jamming, spin glasses and random
constraint satisfaction problems. More recently, he has applied these ideas to
biological fitness landscapes and evolution, connecting sequence variability,
epistasis and evolutionary dynamics.

Bio source: extracted from information sent by the speaker.

### Diego Reforgiato Recupero

**Title:** From Healthcare to Smart Grids: Exploring Optimization Problems and Quantum Solutions

Diego Reforgiato Recupero is Full Professor of Computer Science at the University
of Cagliari, working on AI, knowledge graphs, semantic web technologies, large
language models, NLP, human-robot interaction and intelligent applications in
energy and healthcare. He leads several AI and semantic web laboratories, chairs
the KGELL COST Action on Knowledge Graphs and Large Language Models, and has broad
experience in European and international research projects.

Bio source: extracted from information sent by the speaker.

### Sergio Consoli

**Title:** On the Minimum Quartet Tree Cost problem for the quartet method of hierarchical clustering

Sergio Consoli is a Scientific Project Officer at the European Commission's Joint
Research Centre, with work spanning digital health, artificial intelligence and
combinatorial optimization. He has published on the Minimum Quartet Tree Cost
problem, including an exact algorithm intended to support benchmarking of
heuristics for the problem.

Bio source: sourced from public internet information:
[JRC Academia.edu](https://jrc.academia.edu/SergioConsoli) and
[Tilburg Research Portal](https://research.tilburguniversity.edu/en/publications/an-exact-algorithm-for-the-minimum-quartet-tree-cost-problem/).
